question_text: An uncompressed colour bitmap uses 24 bits per pixel. Describe how those bits can represent the colour of one pixel.
adaptation_rationale: Original application rewritten to be self-contained; assessed reasoning retained within cited 2027 scope.
solution: Pixel colour is represented by numeric binary-encoded channel intensities.; Eight bits are used for each of red, green and blue.; Combining the three intensities gives the resulting pixel colour, with 256 values per channel.
